verdict.rationale: Simular documents agents that operate computers like a human through the UI, keyboard and mouse, across desktop apps, browsers and terminals. It also says the agent takes over when a saved step breaks because the UI changed, which implies its actions are grounded on the live displayed state. However, no evidence explicitly describes screen capture, screenshots or vision-model input as the perception mechanism, and 'Watch your Sai computers work' describes the user watching, not the agent perceiving. missing for 10: explicit documentation of screen capture or vision input, details of how actions are grounded on on-screen elements, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the agent perceives the live screen (capture or vision input) and grounds its actions on what is actually displayed

citations.quote: An open-source framework for agents that control computers like a human — UI, keyboard, and mouse — across environments.
When a step breaks because the UI changed, the agent takes over from there.
You need to see what a real user sees
Sai works across your entire operating system: desktop apps, web browsers, file systems, and terminals, the way a human would.
